column7: evidence

README.md:88 'to your own `package.json`: `npm install-scripts deny better-sqlite3`.' — `npm install-scripts deny` only matches already-installed packages and returns ENOMATCH otherwise, so a consumer following this pre-install instruction gets no allowScripts entry and the dependency install script runs anyway, the exact outcome the paragraph warns about.

README.md:124 '`npm pkg delete allowScripts`.' — with npm 11.19+/12 unapproved dependency install scripts are blocked by default, so deleting the whole allowScripts block leaves better-sqlite3 unapproved, the node-gyp compile the Termux step depends on is skipped, and the worker cannot load SQLite.

LATEST_SCHEMA_REQUIRED_COLUMNS now declares `character_images: ['message_id',]` but the bootstrap path in src/database/index.ts only ever runs `PRAGMA table_info(characters)` to decide "already latest", so a table the contract claims to require is never verified and migration 24 can be skipped; the final head rewrites the check to iterate every table in the map, confirming the gap.

ChatComposer receives only `canSendPhoto` (constant for a character) and no turn-busy prop, and the camera IconButton's onPress calls `onSendPhoto?.(photo, text ?? '')` whenever `canSendPhoto` is true, so a second capture can enter sendPhoto while isGeneratingResponse is true; no guard exists in the hook at this commit.

The production stream server is created as `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })` in cloud-agent/src/index.ts, so ws's ~100 MiB default applies, and the handler does `agentRunSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(data.toString()))` — the full frame is buffered and parsed before schema validation; the final head sets `maxPayload: MAX_AGENT_RUN_BODY_BYTES` on that server.

The Local SQLite container description asserts "Messages never leave device" while the same diagram documents `Rel(app, cloudagent, "Escalated text chat and live voice", ...)`, so the container note is factually wrong for escalated (and now photo) turns; the final head rewrites the sentence to distinguish local persistence from Cloud Agent transport.

column4: Character avatar images: 1024 WebP master + 256 thumb
column7: The new container says "Character avatar images: 1024 WebP master + 256 thumb" and the app relation only covers avatar upload/download, but this PR routes chat photos (source: 'chat', message_id) through the same pending_upload path in characterImageSyncService, so the diagram understates what lives in the bucket.

The mock renders `React.createElement(RNText, { onPress, disabled }, children)` and RN Text ignores `disabled`, so `fireEvent.press` on the "Send in chat" button fires `onSendPhoto` even at `canSendPhoto={false}`; the existing test only asserts the explanatory text, so the disabled behaviour is untested. The final head makes the mock honour `disabled` and adds the press assertion.

The viewer's only dismissal path is `<Pressable style={styles.viewerBackdrop} onPress={...}>` with no accessibilityRole/Label, and the inner Image uses `viewerImage: { width: '100%', height: '100%' }`, so a screen-reader or keyboard user has no labelled way to close the modal (on web onRequestClose does not fire for Escape); the final head adds a labelled close control and labels the backdrop.

ChatView destructures the hook as `const { messages, sendMessage, sendPhoto, canSendPhoto, escalationState, isGeneratingResponse, activeTool, streamingMessage } = useAIChat({...})` and never reads `error`, while sendPhoto's catch calls `setError(...)`; a failed photo turn (e.g. "This character cannot see photos", network failure) therefore leaves the user with a photo bubble and no failure feedback at all.

The claim is inverted: at line 39 `exportDir.delete();` executes after `await zip(exportDir.uri, zipFile.uri)` (line 35) and after the share await, so the directory is never deleted before the zip completes.

journal.tsx:108 `<View style={styles.split}>` in the isWide branch renders only listPane/readPane/chatPane with no `{confirmElement}`, while the effect at line 63 calls `confirm({ title: 'Saved with warnings', ... })` and then `setComposing(false)` (line 70), so on tablets the warning dialog is never mounted and the stored options also suppress an identical later confirm.

import.tsx:64 `disabled={status !== ''}` is new in this PR, and `runImport` sets status at line 34 then awaits `runModelSmokeTest`/`setModelPath`/`setModelId` (lines 35-43) with no try/catch, so any rejection leaves status nonempty and the picker permanently disabled on this screen.

SkiaGraphCanvas.tsx:75 `wrap: { flex: 1, alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }` centers the `size`x`size` Canvas while the absolute Pressables (lines 61-62, `left`/`top` from node.x/node.y) are positioned against the wrapper's padding box, so whenever the flex wrapper exceeds `size` the hit targets are offset from the drawn nodes.

input.tsx:28 `{...rest}` is spread after `editable={!disabled}` (line 15), and `TextInputProps` includes `editable`, so a caller passing `disabled` together with `editable` gets a field that accepts text while styling and announcing itself as disabled.

The step's own comment claims it will 'bound the overall update with a hard timeout as a safety net', but line 51 runs a bare `update` under `sudo apt-get` with only per-transport `Acquire::http::Timeout=120`/`Acquire::https::Timeout=120` and `Acquire::Retries=0` - there is no wall-clock bound on the update, so the multi-source fetch can still run long enough (the exact 6h stall the comment describes) to hang the job.

`Ok(target) => collect_files(&target, false, out),` — the symlink branch has no depth, name, or is_dir check, and `filter_entry` only excludes by name when `file_type().is_dir()`, so a symlink named `node_modules` (or any nested symlink) is canonicalized and walked, ingesting files the module doc explicitly says are skipped.

`assert_eq!(joined.replace(' ', ""), block.trim().replace(' ', ""));` — byte-accurate replay of `split_oversized_block_spans` on `"word — ".repeat(300)` with max_c=100 shows the end-clamp never fires but `start` does land mid-code-point, so removing the new `is_char_boundary(start)` guard makes the test panic; the test does catch the regression, and the proposed `"—".repeat(300)` variant in fact exercises the end clamp only and drops that start-advance coverage.

The spec claims 'Custom `releaseRules` are evaluated before the defaults and short-circuit on first match' (line 187-188), but @semantic-release/commit-analyzer@13.0.1's lib/analyze-commit.js filters all matching rules and keeps the highest release type (`.filter(...).every((match) => { if (compareReleaseTypes(releaseType, match.release)) { releaseType = match.release; ...`)`, with index.js falling back to DEFAULT_RELEASE_RULES only when that returns undefined - so the 'short-circuit on first match' mechanism description is factually wrong, even though the resulting 'major is unreachable' conclusion still holds.

Line 87 reads `cd src-tauri && cargo test test_note_needs_quoting test_quote_for_note 2>&1 \| tail -20`; cargo accepts only one positional TESTNAME filter, so this invocation errors out before any test runs and the plan's verification step can never report the expected COMPILE ERROR/pass.

Line 720's clean fixture writes frontmatter with no `updated_at`, yet the step-3 scan calls `read_existing_token` on every note, so clean.md yields `NoToken` and the assertion `assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1)` on the next line would see two hits.

The stale-update contract still said 'If target file exists but has no `updated_at` (legacy/bootstrap): accept the write', directly contradicting the 2026-09-25 amendment in the same section that refuses such files with `invalid_frontmatter:existing_unparsable:no_token`.

tests/test_ct_doctor.py:467 runs `[sys.executable, str(self.DOCTOR), "--self-test", "check"]`, a form that plain `parse_args` already accepted before this change (verified: `parse_known_args(['--self-test','check'])` gives self_test=True, and `check --self-test` only became tolerable with the new parser), so the suite named 'test_self_test_flag_wins_over_subcommand' does not exercise the post-subcommand behavior the diff added.

tests/test_install.py:204 `self.junk_pycache = PLUGIN_SRC / "scripts" / "__pycache__"` where `PLUGIN_SRC = (REPO / "integrations" / "hermes").resolve()` is the live repository checkout, and the following mkdir/write create junk inside it; `_cleanup_junk` only removes the `.git` dir, so the `__pycache__` fixture is never removed, dirtying the working tree and breaking on read-only or parallel checkouts despite the class docstring claiming 'the source itself must never be modified'.

integrations/hermes/scripts/ct_doctor.py:628 `args, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(argv)` discards leftovers, so a typo like `check --jsno` now silently falls through to `cmd_check(json_output=args.json)` and prints text output instead of exiting 2 with an argument error — confirmed by running argparse: `parse_known_args(['check','--jsno'])` returns `(Namespace(command='check', self_test=False, json=False), ['--jsno'])`.

`m = re.match(r"^(\d+) tools listed", mcp_result.detail)` never matches the zero-tool detail "sidecar answered tools/list with 0 tools - broken install", so tool_count becomes None and check_version_compat skips the live-surface cross-check, emitting PASS for a discoverable version over a known-bad surface.

`if _TOKEN_RE.match(value):` raises TypeError on a non-TEXT SQLite value, and census_source_refs catches only sqlite3.Error despite its 'never raises' contract, so a dynamically-typed imported brain aborts ct_doctor check.

`grep -qE "^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+${PLUGIN_NAME}[[:space:]]*$" "$CONFIG_FILE"` scans every YAML list in the file, so an entry under plugins.disabled satisfies has_plugin_enabled and the installer wrongly reports the plugin (and its skills/hook) as active.

`- uses: actions/checkout@v4` leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config while later steps execute repository-controlled Python (`python -m unittest discover`, an inline heredoc) on pull_request, letting a PR read and exfiltrate the token; `permissions: contents: read` limits scope but not disclosure.

Line 37 is `│       ├── plugin.yaml            # Hermes native plugin manifest (§4)` and the following lines render `│       │   ├── hooks/`, `skills/`, and `scripts/` as children of that file entry; a manifest cannot contain directories, so the spec documents a layout that does not exist and would mislead implementers about the plugin paths.

Line 96 is `rm -f "${DEST_DIR}/plugin.json" "${DEST_DIR}/hooks/hooks.json"`; the earlier comment only claims 'plugin-owned dir, so pruning here never touches user files', but if a user has symlinked `${DEST_DIR}/hooks` (e.g. to a dotfiles checkout) `rm -f` resolves through the link and deletes `hooks.json` outside `${DEST_DIR}`, and `cp -R` also writes through it.

At affcdee the `files` array is ["dist", "LICENSE", "README.md"] but `git ls-tree affcdee -- packages/core-llm-tools` shows no LICENSE or README.md (siblings packages/core and packages/react do have both), so the published tarball would ship with no license/readme and the declared entries are dead.

The package sets publishConfig.access public at affcdee, yet .releaserc.json:14 syncs only ['core','react','expo','prisma-outbox'] and .github/workflows/release.yml:96-99 publishes only those four, so core-llm-tools would never reach npm despite declaring itself publishable; the final head adds it to both.

README line 40 is `import { AgentToolManifest } from '@equationalapplications/core-llm-tools';` while src/index.ts:1 re-exports it as `export type`, so under verbatimModuleSyntax (set in playground/tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json) the documented example fails with TS1484 because AgentToolManifest is used only in a type position.

types.ts declares `type: 'object' \| 'string' \| 'number' \| 'boolean' \| 'array'` while `properties: Record<string, unknown>;` is mandatory, so a string/array schema forces a meaningless `properties` and array `items` cannot be expressed; ed19b22 narrows the union to 'object'.

`git push origin "$BRANCH" "refs/tags/v${RELEASE_VERSION}" --force` updates the release branch and the release tag as two independent ref updates, so a failure on the tag (the exact orphan-tag scenario the surrounding comment describes) can leave the branch up but the tag missing, and Phase 2 - which relocates the tag - then has nothing to work with while Phase 1 still reports success; `git push --atomic` makes both refs land or neither.

Line 529 `(error as any).cause = pendingRankerFallbackError;` performs an unguarded property write on the attacker-supplied `err` (proven only by `err instanceof Error`, which says nothing about a throwing/frozen `cause` setter); in a strict-mode ES module the write throws and escapes this very catch block, defeating the hardening the surrounding try/catch and safeErrorToString calls exist to provide, and `sanitizeRankerError` guards its analogous `name` write.

Line 613 `typeName = errLike ? (errLike.constructor?.name ?? 'Error') : typeof err;` type-annotates a `string` but stores whatever a redefined `constructor` getter returns, so a non-string value flows unguarded into the template literals at lines 632/638 (`VectorRanker ${typeName} ...`) outside any try, where implicit ToString invokes a hostile `toString` and throws out of `sanitizeRankerError`, violating its documented non-throwing contract; the same hole exists for `causeName` at line 624/628.

Line 59 is `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS && install -m 755 system-one-reviewer ~/.local/bin/`, and `install` does not create the destination directory, so a first-time user without ~/.local/bin gets a hard `No such file or directory` failure in the documented first-install path (same at line 64).

Line 72 instructs `export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...`; when the user substitutes the real key it becomes part of the command line and is persisted in the interactive shell history file, leaking a live credential — the README already bothers with `chmod 600` on the file variant, so the history exposure is an inconsistency.

Line 75 `chmod 600 ~/.config/jev-review/.env` runs only after the preceding `echo 'TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...' > .../.env` created the file under the caller's default umask (typically 0644), leaving a window in which other local users can read the key; the read path at system_one_reviewer.py:108-127 does consume this file as the key source.

`return json.loads(r.stdout)` returns the payload without inspecting the top-level `errors` array, so a 200-with-errors response either nulls `data['repository']` (TypeError that escapes main's `except cl.CorpusError`) or silently yields partial PR data.

`cursor = conn["pageInfo"]["endCursor"]` assigns the cursor unconditionally, so a null or unchanged endCursor with hasNextPage true re-requests the same page and, since the default limit is None, loops forever.

`"kind": "positive" if bugs else "clean"` is computed from the pre-verification `bugs` list, so a sample whose every real-bug row is dropped at lines 360-362 is still emitted as a positive with no ground-truth issues.

`prs.append({...})` runs before the per-candidate `verify(...)` loop, and `_verify_via_cache` lets `cl.ensure_commit`/`ensure_clone` CorpusError propagate instead of returning it as an error string, so a PR row is emitted for a head that could not be resolved.

`if os.path.exists(spec["out"]) and not force: continue` skips a run based on the output file alone, so a run whose ledger record was deleted is never re-executed and score_corpus then reports it missing.
